journey.title: Tab out of the visit date into the access notes
journey.goal: Pressing Tab in the open date field moves focus to the next form field so the user can keep typing

functionalJourney.title: Pick a visit date with the pointer
functionalJourney.goal: Clicking a day in the calendar fills the visit date field

guards.title: Pick the next day with arrow keys
guards.goal: Arrow keys move the calendar focus and Enter commits the date

plan.root_cause: The datepicker's keydown listener prevents the default Tab action when the picker is open, causing focus to be lost instead of moving to the next form field.
plan.repair_strategy: Modify the keydown listener in Datepicker.js to allow the Tab key to propagate when the datepicker is active, preserving default focus traversal while keeping other keyboard shortcuts intact.
plan.expected_accessibility_effect: Users can now press Tab to move focus from the visit date field to the access notes field while the datepicker is open, enabling keyboard-only navigation through the form.
functional_risks: Potential interference with any custom Shift+Tab handling (though only Tab is altered).
If other code relied on Tab being suppressed to keep focus inside the picker, that behavior will change.
verification_requirements: Verify that Tab moves focus from #visit-date to #notes when the datepicker is open.
Verify that ArrowRight and Enter still change the date as expected.
Verify that Escape still closes the picker.
Verify that Tab behaves normally when the picker is closed.

plan.root_cause: The datepicker's picker element is inserted into the DOM immediately after the date input field. Its controls (previous/next buttons, view switch, today/clear buttons) are in the default tab order. When the user presses Tab from the date input, the browser moves focus to the first focusable element in the picker (the previous button) instead of the next form field (access notes). Additionally, the datepicker's keydown listener calls onKeydown for Tab, which may further manipulate focus within the picker.
plan.repair_strategy: 1. Modify the keydown listener in Datepicker.js to allow the Tab key to propagate (by not calling onKeydown) when the picker is active, preserving default focus traversal. 2. Remove the picker controls from the tab order by setting tabindex=-1 on them in Picker.js. This ensures Tab skips the picker entirely and moves to the next form field, while arrow key navigation within the picker (handled by onKeydown) remains functional because it does not rely on the controls being in the tab order.
plan.expected_accessibility_effect: Users can now press Tab to move focus from the visit date field directly to the access notes field while the datepicker is open, enabling keyboard-only navigation through the form without being trapped in the datepicker popup. Arrow keys still navigate the datepicker as expected.
functional_risks: If other code relies on the picker controls being in the tab order (unlikely), that behavior will change.
The keydown listener change only affects Tab; all other keys (ArrowRight, Enter, Escape, etc.) continue to be handled by onKeydown.
verification_requirements: Verify that Tab moves focus from #visit-date to #notes when the datepicker is open.
Verify that ArrowRight and Enter still change the date as expected (regression guard).
Verify that Escape still closes the picker.
Verify that Tab behaves normally when the picker is closed.
